recorded: 2026-11-15, after job 1145779 (coupling_scores.py) was SUBMITTED and BEFORE any of its output was seen.
status: [PROVISIONAL: single seed] for every new run -- seed 42 fr_ft, 40 facts about 2 entities.
why: Supervisor meeting 2026-11-13: replace language-specific conclusions with a model-based, language-free account. Experiment D (Plan 5 round 2) showed the top-layer locus is a symptom. Proposed reading: unlearning on D_u removes the target -- durably -- in proportion to how strongly D_u's likelihood is coupled to the target's under theta.

scores.primary: COS_SUM = cos(sum_i grad L(D_u,i), sum_i grad L(fr,i)) at fr_ft over all parameters: the direction a full-batch unlearning step takes, against the target's.
scores.secondary: CARRY = per-fact carry-over (lp_fr_ft - lp_fr_retain, mean over facts); COS_FACT = mean per-fact cosine; per-layer cosines (descriptive).
scores.controls: ctl_retain_fr, ctl_retain_ja: retain rows with no forget fact. A forget source whose COS_SUM does not exceed the higher control has no fact-specific coupling at first order.

check_0_consistency.rule: Descriptive, on the five languages already run (Stage 3, TR-matched, seed 42; recovery order on P(gold): fr < en < ru < id < ja; en vs ja robust, id/fr/ru middle within noise). PASS if COS_SUM(en) > COS_SUM(ja) (en is the more coupled of the two). Also reported, not gating: how far each exceeds the higher retain control. The middle (id, ru) is NOT used: its order is within scoring noise.
check_0_consistency.on_fail: If COS_SUM(ja) >= COS_SUM(en), first-order gradient alignment does not carry the en/ja difference; report that, fall back to CARRY for the gates below, and say the coupling reading rests on carry-over alone.

gate_romaji.rule: Run the romaji arm iff |COS_SUM(romaji) - COS_SUM(ja)| >= 0.5 * |COS_SUM(en) - COS_SUM(ja)| (the swap of script moves coupling at least half the en-ja gap). Same rule on CARRY if check_0 failed.
gate_romaji.prediction_if_run: Token-distribution reading: romaji relearns closer to the en depth curve than to the ja curve (Fig 18) at its stop depth. Language reading: it stays on the ja curve.
gate_romaji.on_fail: Not run. Report: changing the script alone does not change coupling at first order -- itself evidence that 'language' here is not just the token IDs.

new_language_arm.choice: Among ko / hi / ar / fa / iw (all non-Latin scripts), run the ONE with the HIGHEST COS_SUM. This separates script from coupling: a non-Latin script with high coupling is predicted durable (en-like); the 'non-Latin = fragile' reading predicts ja-like. If the highest is still below COS_SUM(ja) + 0.5 * gap, the arm cannot separate the two readings and is reported as such (run anyway, labelled weak).
new_language_arm.prediction: Relearned French P(gold) at its stop sits on the side of the midpoint between the en and ja depth curves (Fig 18, interpolated at its stop depth) that its COS_SUM falls on relative to the en-ja midpoint of COS_SUM.

arm_recipe: plan3_arm.sbatch unchanged except --lang: gradient difference, forget AND retain term in the arm's language (romaji: forget01 + retain99 romanised with the same make_romaji.py conversion), floor none, lr 5e-6, cap 50 epochs, stop at the first epoch with French P(gold) <= 0.470 (between en 0.49 and ja 0.44 at the Stage 3 TR match; P(gold) is the primary metric since Plan 5 1b). Fallback: one rerun at lr 1.5e-5 if not reached; no other retries. Then benign relearn on retain99, French and English columns, 3 epochs.
primary_outcome: Relearned French P(gold), each column, read against the en and ja depth curves of Fig 18 at the arm's stop depth (not against fixed midpoints: Experiment D showed fixed midpoints mislead when depth differs).
known_limitations: Romaji is automatic (pykakasi 2.3.0): some kanji readings wrong; topic particle written 'ha' not 'wa'.
First-order alignment at theta_0 ignores how coupling changes along the unlearning trajectory.
New-language translations are Farashah et al.'s (Google Translate + native-speaker QC on 100 instances per language).
One seed, one model, one method; 2 entities.

npo_arms.recorded: 2026-11-15, before either NPO arm was submitted.
npo_arms.why: Supervisor 2026-11-13: test the key conclusions under the NPO family. Tongyao expects little change (the gradient still enters at the last layer).
npo_arms.method: NPO+RT exactly as Zhang et al. 2024 (arXiv 2404.05868) on TOFU: L = -(2/beta) E log sigmoid(-beta log[pi_theta(y|x)/pi_ref(y|x)]) + NLL(retain), pi = full-sequence probability, beta = 0.1, pi_ref = the model before unlearning (fr_ft), peak lr 1e-5 (their TOFU value), effective batch 32, AdamW wd 0.01, linear warm-up + linear decay. The same beta is used by Wei et al. (NeurIPS 2025, 'following previous literature') and open-unlearning's released TOFU NPO checkpoints. Variants seen in our papers folder and NOT used: Hu et al. beta 0.01; Farashah et al. beta 1; Xiang et al. pi_ref = the BASE model + KL retain term.
npo_arms.deviations_from_zhang: Our harness, kept identical to the gradient-difference arms so only the loss changes: LR schedule built for 50 epochs with warmup ratio 0.2 (theirs: 10 epochs, 1 warm-up epoch), stopped at matched depth; retain term in the arm's language; adamw_torch with optimizer offload (32-bit).

runs.en: env METHOD=npo STOP_PGOLD=0.470 sbatch plan3_arm.sbatch en 1.0e-5
runs.ja: env METHOD=npo STOP_PGOLD=0.470 sbatch plan3_arm.sbatch ja 1.0e-5

npo_arms.fallback: An arm that does not reach P(gold) 0.470 by epoch 50 (NPO's forget weight shrinks as pi_theta falls below pi_ref, so it can plateau) gets ONE rerun at lr 2e-5; otherwise reported as 'NPO cannot reach matched depth for this language'.

predictions.H_npo_gap: At matched French P(gold), the ja NPO arm relearns to a HIGHER French P(gold) than the en NPO arm by more than the gradient-difference seed spread (0.035) in BOTH relearn columns, and each sits within 0.05 of its own language's gradient-difference depth curve (Fig 18) at that depth.
predictions.H_npo_regime: Own-language damage regime replicates: near-certain own-language tokens (fr_ft log p > -0.1) lose > 10 nats in the ja arm and < 5 nats in the en arm at the stop.
predictions.reading: both -> the key conclusions are not specific to gradient difference; H_npo_gap only -> durability gap survives but the damage regime is GD-specific (NPO is bounded); neither -> report the method dependence.

npo_arms.primary_outcome: relearned French P(gold), each column, against the en / ja depth curves at the stop depth.

coupling_round1.result: Raw COS_SUM (summed-gradient cosine with the French target): en -0.086, id -0.091, ru -0.072, ja -0.096, ko -0.086, hi -0.060, ar -0.069, fa -0.052, iw -0.053, romaji -0.071; controls: retain fr +0.064, retain ja -0.098. Per-fact means all within +-0.025. CARRY: en 0.64, id 0.65, ru 0.37, ja 0.18, ko 0.31, hi 0.06, ar 0.33, fa 0.12, iw 0.28, romaji -0.04.
coupling_round1.validity: FAILED. COS_SUM is dominated by a language-wide direction (mostly layers 0-11): every non-French text, forget or retain, is negative, and Japanese retain rows with no forget fact match the Japanese forget set. By the scores.controls rule no forget source exceeds the higher control. The nominal gate outcomes (check_0 en > ja by 0.010; romaji gate passes; highest new language fa) are therefore NOT acted on.
coupling_round1.amendment_decided_after_seeing_data: Round 2 (coupling_scores.py --contrast): each language gets its own control (the same 40 strided retain99 rows in that language; romaji: the same rows romanised) and the primary score becomes CONTRAST_SUM = cos(sum_i [g(forget_L,i) - g(ret_L,i)], sum_i [g(forget_fr,i) - g(ret_fr,i)]); CONTRAST_FACT = the per-fact mean with ret row i paired to fact i. Unit-tested (identical source -> 1.0; forget == control -> zero gradient).

gates_restated_before_round2_output.validity: A language shows fact-specific coupling at first order iff CONTRAST_SUM > 0. If neither en nor ja does, first-order gradient alignment is reported as not carrying the en/ja difference and the gates fall back to CARRY (check_0.on_fail).
gates_restated_before_round2_output.new_language_arm: the one of ko / hi / ar / fa / iw with the highest CONTRAST_SUM (CARRY if check_0 fails).
gates_restated_before_round2_output.no_arm_without_user: Arms selected by these gates are proposed to the user before submission.
